text:
anya: heads up — after the kernel-binning change deployed at 1711123000 we're seeing a ~12% drop in prefix/prompt cache hit rate for the 8k cohort. noticed on 3 clusters (us-west-2-prod*).

sam: ugh, noticed latency tails bump too?

anya: p90 tokens/sec down ~8%, p99 latency up ~30ms. TTL eviction spikes during warmup windows.

leo: ran a quick profile. attaching inline summary: 
```
# cache profile (last 12h)
cohort  hit_rate  requests  avg_ttl  evictions
4k      0.87      1.1M      2.1m     4.2k
8k      0.71      980k      1.2m     18.3k  <-- regression
16k     0.89      420k      3.5m     1.0k
```

leo: key observation: kernel-binning changed kernel selection at ~seq_len 6000 which increased KV lookup fragmentation: more keys hashed into larger slab buckets, raising clobber/eviction rate.

kai: GPU mem fragmentation went up after deploy, per-gpu free segments dropped (avg free segments 12 -> 6). suggests bigger allocation churn.

infra-bot: deploy 1711123000 by sam completed 2024-03-18T16:45:02Z. config: kernel-binning-v2, small-prefill-enabled.

sam: quick hypothesis: kernel thresholds moved some long prompts into a kernel path that increases temporary allocation size (kv slot size change), which triggers LRU eviction sooner. combined with our aggressive soft-ttl defaults = higher churn.

anya: can we validate delta by toggling kernel-binning on a canary? also want experiment where we increase cpu-side cache reserve and lower soft-ttl to reduce thrashing.

leo: propose 2 experiments (each 2h window):
- EXP A: rollback kernel-binning-v2 on canary (compare hit_rate + p99).
- EXP B: keep kernel-binning-v2, but bump cpu_cache_reserved from 0.12 -> 0.2 and reduce soft_ttl from 30s -> 8s (we think shorter soft-ttl reduces stale large prefix retention and lowers fragmentation).

sam: also add a slab compaction pass every 60s for the canary to reclaim tiny free segments (low-cost GC).

kai: note: compaction has small perf cost on hot GPUs, but for canary should be fine. compaction PR: https://git.redwood.ai/r/redwood/infra/pull/4321

leo: to reproduce locally:
```
# simulate workload
./tools/kv-sim --profile --seq-dist=8k-heavy --kernel=binning-v2 --ttl=30s --cpu-reserve=0.12
# for experiment B
./tools/kv-sim --kernel=binning-v2 --ttl=8s --cpu-reserve=0.2 --slab-compact-interval=60
```

anya: timelines — can we run EXP A tomorrow 09:00 UTC? sam/leo to own. EXP B after we have baseline results.

sam: yes, I can flip canary and collect traces + pprof. will annotate with trace IDs.

leo: I'll add detailed hit-rate dashboards sliced by model, seq_len buckets, and kernel path. also add eviction-reason breakdown (ttl vs lru vs frag).

kai: if EXP B reduces evictions we may tune global defaults: cpu_reserve -> 0.18, soft_ttl -> 10s, slab_compact interval -> 120s. but verify perf cost.

anya: fallback plan if canary fails: immediate rollback cluster-wide and revert kernel-binning-v2. ops notified.

infra-bot: pageralert channel alerted if p99 latency > 4s for 5m on prod clusters.

sam: assigning: sam -> run EXP A and collect traces; leo -> dashboards and simulation; kai -> validate compaction PR on canary; anya -> coordinate rollback plan.

anya: thanks all. will post short RCA if EXP A reproduces. :thumbsup:
